elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative language permits Customer to terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience,” including in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate on thirty days’ prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 applies after termination and refunds prepaid recurring Fees for the post-termination period, but it does not refund all prepaid “Fees,” which also include professional-services, usage, and other amounts under the supplied definition.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty days, not 60 to 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the rendered language, so the condition requiring a cap is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly prohibited from terminating for convenience during a committed term, and no broader Vendor convenience-termination right is granted elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no requirement that Vendor provide 90 days’ notice; it only prohibits Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
